cases.title: Terms list with string ids, windows and status labels.
(BE-3RD-08): the one-form create and update of a Term are gone; Terms are built with the wizard (its per-field checks: TC-CFG-020; its publish rules: TC-CFG-034, which replaced TC-CFG-004).
Room Types with inventory counts; mutual invite only for 2 Beds; names are unique.
changing the Beds of a Room Type adds or retires Beds in its Rooms.
Room Classes show where they are used and the deposit rate; the surcharge is bounded.
fees and refund rules save as one document; a new rule gets an id; bad rates are refused. The seven refund triggers of spec §9 are there (V10, V42).
(M3): the refund of a rejected Application cannot be switched off: the rejection path needs it (400 RULE_REQUIRED); its percent may still change.
criteria switches and priority groups (order, new group, member counts).
weights must total 100%; saving creates the next snapshot; a dry run allocates nothing.
system parameters are typed; an invalid value is named by its key.
Admin › Utility loads with its option lists, rejects values outside them and audits a change.
(permission): a Manager cannot open Admin configuration.
the demo tools are off unless the server turns them on (DEMO_TOOLS); a reset is refused.
the Admin lists the furniture types with their items, adds one (code and names checked, the code fixed afterwards) and cannot make a type a Room Class requires standard; other roles are refused.
each Room Class lists the furniture it requires; the Admin replaces a class's requirements, only with active class-defining types and sensible quantities, and conformance follows at once.

each furniture type is personal (furniture, one per Bed) or shared by the Room (appliances and fixtures) and has a real price (0–1,000,000,000 VND, empty while not set); four condition levels give the share of that price an item is still worth (100, 75, 50, 0 %). The Admin sets the price and adds, renames, revalues or removes levels (a Vietnamese name, the English one optional, 0–100 %, listed best first); Managers may not.

the four condition levels the room handover records its conditions on (Intact, Partly damaged, More than half damaged, Completely damaged) cannot be removed; renaming them or changing their value is allowed.

each group lists its settings with where they act; an out-of-range value is refused; a saved change is audited and announced to students; grouped settings left System parameters; only the Admin edits.

Who may apply gives the students failing each check now and the checks without a switch; weights read as levels and save from levels (Very important counts twice); the dry run of four approved Applications shows the draft next to the rules in use, with an example Room.
the list holds back-office accounts only, with labels and string ids; filters by role and Block.
an invited Staff sets the password from the emailed link (one use only), signs in with the Block scope, and a password change keeps the current session but signs out the others.
(negative): invite validation names each field.
disabling a user signs them out at once and is written to the Audit Log.
(negative): the Admin cannot lock themselves out.
(permission): Staff cannot open Admin screens.
the permission matrix is the enforced rule table.
Audit Log filters, labels and retention; a bad range is refused.

the Admin writes a pinned announcement for all students; a student reads it at the top of the board and in the bell, unread; marking it read in the bell (id {@code ann-…}) updates both; the Admin sees one read.

Staff write only to the residents of their Blocks: everybody or another Block is refused; the residents of the Block read it and other students do not; Staff end their own announcement; students cannot write one.
a change of the Deposit (Admin) and of a Block's settings (Manager) become change announcements with the old and new values, in both languages; a Block's change reaches only its residents.
the student's Term is the open one; catalog prices and eligibility for it.
submit with a Deposit Invoice, then the list, detail, Home and notification; a second one is refused.
(negative): a contact field given must be valid; consent and roommate rules are named per field.
the wizard no longer asks for a contact (R-16): an Application without one is accepted and its snapshot is the contact on the student's profile, which stays as it was.
(privacy): the same answer for every unusable code, and a limited number of checks.
(business rule): an invited pair reaches the office together: the first to pay waits as Awaiting Roommate; both are Submitted when the second Deposit is paid.
a declined invitation leaves the inviter matched automatically.
cancelling voids an unpaid Deposit; a paid one is refunded by the rule; the student may apply again.
(job): an unpaid Application expires when its Deposit window passes; its Invoice is voided.
(permission): Staff cannot use student screens; another student's Application is 404.

The stay length (spec §6.6, D-13) is 1 to stay.max_terms, capped by the semesters the student has left (stay.program_semesters); it is kept on the Application and shown to the student and the back office; a student who already holds a Bed for the Term cannot apply (not a continuing resident).
the queue, the review view (opening it starts the review), rejection needs a note, once only.
(scope): every Manager sees every Block's Applications (ADR-19); Staff and students cannot review.

the Manager approves in bulk, runs, resolves the conflict to the waitlist and commits the Block, which approves it at once (ADR-19): Allocations, Balance Invoices, notifications and My Room. Staff cannot commit.
a dry run is a preview; students and Staff cannot use runs (ADR-19).

a student's question reaches the model with the guide in the student's language and the student's own data (their Room, without the check-in pass); the model's answer is returned; the question, a follow-up too, is preceded by a reminder of the language and to answer from the data.
the conversation is checked (not empty, roles user or assistant, ending with a question, at most 2000 characters a message) and only students may use the assistant.
a question about the door code, in Vietnamese with or without accents or in English, gets the fixed answer pointing to My Room without asking the model, which could make a code up.

the assistant answers in the language the student writes in: a question with Vietnamese letters gets the Vietnamese guide and reminder even on an English screen; a question without them follows the screen's language.

an answer with Chinese characters is never shown: the model is asked once more with its answer and a request to write it in the student's language; if it still has them, the student gets 503 ASSISTANT_NO_ANSWER.
a student may ask the configured number of questions per hour, then gets 429.
without a model server the status says off and a question answers 503 ASSISTANT_OFFLINE.
valid credentials return a token and the contract user shape.
wrong password and unknown email get the same generic answer.
me works with the token; after sign-out the same token gets 401.
no token → 401; a student calling an Admin endpoint → 403.
(boundary): the 5th wrong password locks the account, even for the right password.
(negative): body validation returns field messages.
published Terms with string ids, ISO dates and the list total.
forgot password never reveals whether the email exists.
"remember" may be left out (Jackson 3 would reject a missing primitive).
(negative): Google sign-in needs exactly one of code and credential.
(negative): the redirect flow is accepted only for the web app's own sign-in page; any other address is refused before Google is asked.
without Google configuration both flows answer 503 GOOGLE_SIGN_IN_DISABLED.
(security): Spring's default in-memory user is not created, so no generated password is written to the log; sign-in goes only through CampusStay's accounts.
the Block's settings and the Admin limits; the Manager saves a change, which is audited.
(negative): values outside the Admin limits or out of order are named per field; Manager only.
the house rules are saved without desk hours (review R-08: no longer asked); the stored desk hours stay as they were.
the Block's staff with titles, handles, Blocks, open work and duty; the summary.
a Manager sets what a Staff member of any Block handles (ADR-19); duty is not set by hand.
a Staff member reads their own duty, request types and workload (A-60); signing in put them on duty, and students may not read it.
the Manager asks Admin for a new account in the Block; one waiting request per email.
the Admin sees the stages, the scenario accounts and the sample files; nobody else does.
a reset needs a known stage and RESET typed, and refuses a database without the base data.
the sample files download as CSV with a byte-order mark; an unknown one is 404.
the Balance includes the Utility Deposit; until it is paid the desk blocks check-in; then the student checks in with the hand-over items, once only.
(scope): another Block's Staff do not find the student, every Manager does (ADR-19); students and the Admin have no desk.

check-out settles the Utility Deposit: the share since the Room's last reading, the damage charge, the refund to the Manager; the Bed is free again, the figures stay as settled and the Room's door code must change.

the desk enters the final meter readings Room by Room, typed or from the XLSX template, before the leavers come: each Room's reading goes to the check-out drafts of its leavers; a Room without leavers in the user's Blocks or a reading below the Room's last one is reported and not saved.
when the charges exceed the Utility Deposit, the rest is invoiced to the student.

check-out records the damage of each furniture item of the Room (spec §6.16): the damage charge is their sum, a damaged item becomes Broken with the reason in its history, an item of another Room is refused; the list shows the Term's check-out date and whether a leaver is past it.
register, register again, unregister; the token is stored by hash and validated.
a notification is pushed to the user's devices after commit; an expired token is disabled.
Staff draw a random code, read it to set the lock, confirm it, and it becomes the Room's code; the database holds it encrypted and every view is in the Audit Log.
(validation, scope, permission): codes are 6 new digits; other Blocks and other roles are refused.
a CSV of Rooms and codes is checked line by line; a correct file proposes every code at once.
when a resident leaves a Room its code must change: a task opens once, the Block's Staff are told, and confirming the new code closes it and tells the remaining residents (never the code itself).

a student whose Balance is paid and whose check-in start has come waits for the Room's code; once Staff confirm it, it is released to them (spec §6.8): they are told (never the code), see it and become a resident; without a Bed there is nothing to show.
an unassigned request escalates, then passes its timer; the Manager reassigns it once.
an escalation closes by itself once the request is back on track.
an undecided next-Term Room-Change Request escalates; the Manager offers a temporary Bed; Manager only.
a Manager creates a Draft (fields checked; Staff may not), publishes it and the Block's residents are told; a published Family Day cannot be edited; Staff of another Block cannot read it.

a resident registers guests for one time slot and each guest gets their own pass; guests are checked (a child comes with an adult, at most the Family Day's number); one registration per student; students of other Blocks and students who live nowhere cannot see or register.
a time slot never takes more guests than its places: a registration larger than what is left is refused, and two students racing for the last place get it once.

at the desk, Staff of the Block scan a pass, check the identity paper and let the guest in once; the guest leaves and the pass no longer works; Staff of another Block cannot use it; an unknown pass is refused and written to the Audit Log.
two desks scanning the same pass at the same moment let the guest in once.

after the time slots a guest still inside is Overdue and a guest who never came is a No-show; the Manager cannot close the day while someone is inside; Staff close the visit with a note; closing records the No-shows and the counts.

a student cancels before their time slot and the places come back; a Manager cancels a registration with a reason and the student is told; cancelling the Family Day cancels every registration, the passes stop working and the students are told.
registration closes at its time: a published Family Day whose registration is over takes nobody.

(contract A-71): guests still inside after their time slot. The desk reminds every student concerned in one batch (one notification each, sent again while guests stay); a student confirms their guests are safe; Staff check out a confirmed guest and must wait for the others; nothing to remind or confirm before the slot ends.

(contract A-71): Family Day statistics. The Block's Staff, Managers and the Admin read the figures of a Family Day (registrations, guests registered and arrived, time slots, the overdue procedure) and the overview of the Family Days that are over; Staff of another Block and students cannot; a Draft has none.

an unpaid charge past its due date becomes Overdue (the student is told) while a Balance past its deadline does not (it is forfeited instead, spec §6.6); a Manager sees the charge with the days overdue and sends a reminder, in-app and by email.
refunds wait for the Block Manager; rejecting needs a note; the student is told.

a refund lists its rule's percentage apart from its amount (R-21); a Manager reminds a student without a refund account to enter it, once a day, not once it is entered (R-19); the student sees their refunds on Payments (R-24).
(scope): items of the Blocks in scope, with counts per status and filters; other Blocks are refused.
(permission): Managers register items with new asset codes; Staff cannot; the input is checked.

(business rule): Staff move items inside their Block now (status follows the place, the Room's conformance changes); moving to another Block is a Manager's transfer, planned and then done by Staff; a planned move can also be cancelled.

(business rule): the stock per Block counts the store, the Rooms and broken items and values the store at the types' real prices; another Block is refused to Staff. A personal item that leaves its Room loses its Bed and gets a free Bed of the Room it is moved back to.
(validation): status changes follow the place, Disposed is final, and every change is recorded.

without the Room's door code the start is refused and the condition says why; once the code is set the student starts the inventory, receives the code and is a resident, but Utility does not count yet.
while the check-in inventory is on, the desk does not check in a new resident who has not filed it; once the inventory is final the student is checked in by it.
the student's view never carries the Room's record nor the comparison, and the Staff endpoints are closed to students.
an inventory that matches the Room's record is final at once: Utility counts from the student's reading and the desk check-in is recorded; a reading lower than the Room's is refused.
with the student in the Room, Staff sign the Final report there: the inventory is final at once (no agreement on the app), the student is checked in, and check-out compares with that Final report.
a meter far above the Room's record is a major difference: Staff ask for a visit, record what they find and send it; the student agrees with a comment and the inventory is final (no dispute state).
a draft past its deadline becomes final with the Room's record; Utility counts from the code.
at check-out a personal item Good at check-in and Damaged now costs its price × the share the Mostly damaged level loses (50 %); the check-out waits for the student's agreement on the app.
damage to a shared item is charged only once the student acknowledges it; a declined one is not.

damage Staff record on a shared item at a check-out is split evenly among the Room's residents: the leaver's line carries their share (with the rounding remainder), and when the check-out is completed each roommate gets a DAMAGE Invoice for theirs, which becomes Overdue like any charge when it is not paid in time.
the seeded checklist; a Draft is published as v1; editing publishes v2 and keeps v1 as Replaced.

a schedule starts its first run at once and notifies residents; Staff record the Rooms with their own checks (people, furniture), a failed item creates a Maintenance Request with the severity's priority (a failed furniture item one that names it); the run is submitted; the job starts the next.

Staff see every run assigned to them (not only the first), open one by its code, and add photos of a furniture item and of the meters like a student's check-in inventory; Managers list every Block's schedules and runs, each with its Block, without the editor options.
archiving a checklist pauses its schedules, which cannot resume until another is published.
(permission): schedules are the Managers', for every Block (ADR-19); runs need Staff.
Blocks with their Floors, Room counts per Room Type and closed Rooms.
a new Block gets the standard layout; generating again adds nothing; bad ranges are refused.
(scope): Staff see only their Blocks; a Block outside the scope is refused.
a Floor's Rooms and Beds with the out-of-service details.
(business rule): an occupied Room cannot go out of service, its Block cannot change gender and its Room Type cannot change Beds; the occupant shows on the Bed.
out of service and back, with the reason label, who set it, and the Audit Log.
(permission): students cannot see the inventory; unknown Rooms are 404.

bulk generation gives the new Rooms the Room Class chosen for them (the Floor keeps it as the class of its later Rooms); each Floor lists the classes its Rooms have, which are set per Room from then on.
a Room code list (CSV, with or without its header) gives the Rooms and the codes no Room has.
Staff record the request with evidence; the Block Manager approves a deadline, after which the desk lets the student check in even though the Term's window is closed.
a rejection needs a reason; every Manager sees the request (ADR-19); a student has one late check-in per Term, so the desk cannot record another after the rejection.

the student asks online with a reason, the day and an evidence file, up to the check-in end plus late_check_in.max_days; the Managers are told; one request per Term, also after the decision; a Manager approves at most that day.
the user carries the account's language; the account changes it; only vi and en are accepted.
with Accept-Language: vi errors and field messages are Vietnamese, the code unchanged; English without.
a notification keeps both texts; the Notification Center shows the reader's language.
a checked-in student reports with photos and follows the request; the form is validated.
Staff of the Block assign, plan the visit, post updates and resolve; the student is notified, reopens once and confirms the fix. Photos open through signed links.
only the person in charge changes the status; another Staff member of the Block takes the request over first (recorded in its history), and a Manager may act on any request.
the queue is scoped: another Block's Staff neither see nor count the request; Managers do (ADR-19).
templates with their variables and sample values; the push limit and unknown variables.
a test sends the unsaved text, with sample values, to the signed-in Admin.
options leave system emails out; the preview counts the group and renders the first email.
sending queues one email per student (and the in-app notice with push); validation; Admin only.
the current month opens on first use; Rooms with residents wait for a reading.
a reading may not go back; an unusual jump waits for a confirmation.
a CSV import checks every line before it saves any.
the template lists the period's Rooms with their previous values; filled in Excel with Vietnamese headers it is read back, and Rooms left blank are skipped, not refused.
closing the month issues each resident's Utility Invoice with its breakdown; then it is read-only.

an extension in the Stay's last Term is approved at once (the Bed is kept, the Stay commits more Terms); with an overdue Invoice it waits for Staff, who decide it with a note to reject; the length is checked; the end of the stay releases the next-Term Bed at once; after the request deadline nothing can be filed.
Room Class change requests are gone (user decision 19/11/2026): students cannot ask for one and Staff cannot list or decide one; a Room's class per Term is set by Managers only.

the requests window in one list (room changes, swaps, extensions), oldest first; a bulk decision decides each one in its own transaction and reports those it could not (a kind that does not exist); a bulk rejection needs a reason; Staff of another Block see nothing.
newest first, with the unread count and string ids; {@code limit} caps the items.
mark one read (twice is fine), then all; someone else's notification is 404.
(negative): signed-in users only.

Staff move a resident to another Room of their Block for a reason: both meters are read, the old Room's code must change, the next-Term Bed follows, nothing is charged; the student is told; the moves list shows it; validation, other Blocks and students are refused.

after the next-Term fees are issued, Staff may no longer move a next-Term Bed; a Manager moves an unpaid one and its fee is void and issued again for the new Bed; a paid fee allows only a Bed of the same price.

a new Maintenance Request gets its SLA deadline from the Block's timer (urgent sooner than normal) and may name a furniture item of the Room, which the queue and the detail show; the item's history keeps the repair, reported and resolved; an item of another Room is refused.
the Room hub lists the Room's residents, Maintenance Requests, meter readings and inspections next to its class, furniture and door code; Staff of another Block may not open it.

the back-office search finds students by code or name, Rooms with or without the dash and request codes inside the user's Blocks; Staff of another Block find neither the Room nor its resident; short queries find nothing and students may not search.
the routing rules page lists the Block's staff with their open and finished work.
the Term hub shows the requests window once it opened (open requests, Continuing residents, next-Term fees issued and paid, Beds released) and nothing before.
reset sets the new password, the old one fails and every earlier session is signed out.
(negative): a reset link works only once.
(negative): a weak new password is refused and the link stays usable.
(negative): a wrong current password is a field error and changes nothing.
change keeps the current session, signs out the others and the new password works.
(negative): change refuses a weak new password and keeps the old one.

the claim waits for a Manager and stops the Deposit window (the Application does not expire); the queue lists it with the count and total; a bulk confirmation pays each Invoice at the time of its claim, one audit entry each, and the Applications are submitted; unknown Invoices and claims without their transfer receipt (R-23) are skipped.

a rejection needs a reason; the Invoice is Unpaid again and the deadline continues with the time that was left (at least payment.rejected_claim_min_hours); the student is told; a second rejection cancels the Deposit and the Application expires.

(validation, permission): one claim at a time; a paid or void Invoice and a Deposit past its deadline cannot be claimed; a student cannot cancel while a claim waits; only Managers see the queue and decide; an empty selection is refused; Invoices without a claim are skipped.
a Utility Invoice is a debt: a claim made after its due date leaves the date as it was, a rejection returns it to Overdue and rejections never cancel it.
Balance reminders go out 3 and 1 days before the deadline, once each, never for a claim waiting; the Managers hear once an hour how many claims wait.
Invoices with filters and the summary; every Manager sees every Block, Staff do not (ADR-19).

a Manager confirms one Invoice with the bank reference and its receipt (required, R-23), even a transfer the student did not claim (the claim is recorded in the Manager's name); the Application is submitted; a second confirmation is refused; Staff and students may not confirm (ADR-19, ADR-22).
receipt files are sniffed; a void Invoice (its Application cancelled) cannot be confirmed.
the Deposit Invoice in the list, its detail and the VietQR payment page; the QR can be refreshed.
(permission): another student's Invoice is 404; the Admin may read it.

the enrolled list of the next Term: a continuing resident who graduated (group 1, the directory updated: group 4), a continuing resident missing from the list (group 2), an unknown code (group 3), another student's changed status (group 4); the template; Managers upload, the Admin reads, Staff may not; a file without a student code column is refused.

resolving: a note is required; "Not enrolled" releases the student's Bed for the next Term (told in the app); "Enrolled" keeps everything; an item is resolved once; then nothing blocks the next-Term fees.

a leavers list during a Term: a resident who withdrew gets a termination (reason Not enrolled); an applicant's Application is rejected and the paid Deposit refunded by the rule "Not enrolled" (waiting for a Manager); students not on a leavers list are not questioned.
(BE-3RD-05): a list said "Withdrawn" (the directory followed it); the Manager checks and records "Enrolled": the directory says Enrolled again.
(BE-3RD-06): uploading the corrected list again replaces the first one: its open items close as superseded, so each student has one open item and the counts do not double.

a student reads and saves their refund account; the number keeps its digits only, the bank is chosen from the list by its BIN and the student accepts responsibility for the account (R-22), each field is checked, and only students have one.

the card shows the Term open for registration with its countdown, places and lowest price; its details list the timeline and every price with its Deposit, the furniture its Room Class requires and the Beds of the student's gender (no Rooms); a Draft has no details.

M2 opens the requests window once: a resident with Terms left keeps the Bed as continuing, one in the Stay's last Term as awaiting extension; a student not living in the Room yet and a terminated resident get none. My Room shows the next Term with its price, the students are told, Staff and Managers read the overview, and the new students' assignment of the next Term waits for the request deadline.
M3 closes filing: a Bed still awaiting extension is released (the student is told in-app and by email, with the day to check out), a continuing one stays; the overview counts the ending.

Issue next-Term fees: the preview names what blocks them (filing still open, no reconciliation); once filing closed and the enrolled list is reconciled a Manager issues one fee per continuing resident = 100 % of the next Term's price of the Bed (no Deposit); issuing again charges nobody twice; leavers receive the end-of-stay notice; Staff may not issue; the fee cannot be claimed while Utility is overdue; paid, the Stay counts the next Term.
M7: a next-Term fee unpaid at its deadline with no claim waiting is void and its Bed released (nothing kept); a fee whose claim waits for a Manager keeps the Bed.

the turnover: from the next Term's check-in start a paid continuing resident receives the Room's code and lives in the next Term (the current Term's Allocation ends); a mover's old Room needs a new code; the turnover list shows leavers, movers and the Rooms whose residents change, and Staff record their meter readings.
Staff dashboard: the review queue, Rooms out of service, the Block's Beds, what needs attention.
Block Manager dashboard: occupancy by floor, the SLA rate and target, what is waiting.

the Manager's and the Admin's dashboards report the money of Collections and refunds (a paid Deposit without a Bed included) with what is still owed, residents apart from held Beds, the continuing residents the funnel leaves out, the Staff work a Manager decides, and the values of each attention line.
the Manager's approval counts; Staff may not see them.
Admin dashboard: the Term, people, the funnel, Blocks, configuration checks and integrations.
occupancy by Block, Room Type and Room Class; capacity leaves Rooms out of service out.
money per Block; Deposits of students without a Bed have a row of their own.
the Block report counts check-ins per week and who has not checked in yet.
a Term that has ended still reports who lived there (Allocations ended by check-out, not by a room change), and a refunded Deposit without a Bed counts in the row of its own.
before the first Term is published the dashboards and approval counts answer with empty figures (the Admin's checks still list what to set up); an unknown Term and the reports still answer 404.
exports are CSV files with the screen's columns, written to the Audit Log; scope and permissions.

assigned and unpaid (yellow); paid but before the check-in start, then without a Room code, the student waits (no code); Staff confirm the Room's code and it is released: the student is a resident (orange), is told and sees the code; a student who pays later receives the current code at once.

(business rule): a Balance past its deadline without a claim is forfeited: the Allocation is cancelled, the Balance void, the Application Forfeited, the Deposit kept by the rule "Balance not paid" (a 0 % rule records no refund; a 10 % rule one refund, never two) and the student told; a claim waiting keeps the Bed, and so does a later Balance deadline a Manager chose when approving a late check-in, which may not pass the arrival day (the Balance is paid before check-in).
a Balance whose claims are rejected twice is cancelled with its Allocation (spec §6.7).

the options show the next-Term Bed and the next Term's prices; a request for another Room Type, one open request per window; validation; a student without a Bed kept for the next Term, or in the last Term of the Stay, cannot ask yet.

Staff of the Block approve with a free matching Bed of the next Term: the next-Term Allocation moves there (the student still lives in their Room this Term) and the next-Term fee will be that Bed's price; no Invoice or refund is made; Staff of another Block see nothing; after the next-Term fees the Beds are fixed.
a rejection needs a listed reason; the student sees it; students may not decide.
without a Term the list shows the next Term to start, editable, with each Room's class and its furniture conformance; the running Term is shown as fixed. Staff see their Blocks only.

a Manager sets Rooms' class for Spring 2027; Fall 2026 keeps the old class, the Rooms and Beds screen and the assignment inputs of Spring 2027 use the new one, conformance shows what the class lacks, and every Room's change is in the Audit Log.
(business rule): a running Term keeps its classes, and a Room whose Beds are already given for the Term (an Allocation) keeps its class there, so no price already charged changes.
(permission, validation): only Managers set classes; students cannot read; bad input is named.

and TC-APP-021: three Waitlisted students each get held options in partly filled Rooms. One accepts (Allocated with a Balance), one declines and one does not answer: both are cancelled and their paid Deposits wait as refunds for the Block Manager.

a waitlisted student sees the open offer, the day the waitlist ends and the refund; withdrawing closes the offer, releases its Beds, cancels the Application and asks a Manager to refund the whole Deposit, whose list shows the student's bank account (A-61, A-62). A plain cancel is refused, and only one's own waitlisted Application can be withdrawn.

when the Term's check-in starts, a waitlisted Application without an open offer is cancelled with the whole Deposit to refund and the student is told; one with an open offer keeps it until it is answered.

a Manager runs Round 2 (M8): the Waitlisted students without an open offer get held options on the Term's free Beds, by the rules of the offers made when a Block is approved; students may not run it. The Manager's list shows who is waiting without an offer, then who got one with its options (A-58).
rules, gaps and timers of the Block; validation; Manager only, in scope.
a new Maintenance Request goes to the category rule first, else All; off duty → fallback.
a next-Term Room-Change Request goes to the Block's rule and is due at the decision deadline of its requests window (M4, spec §6.18).
a Manager sets a Staff member's weekly shifts; bad shifts 400; the list shows them; audited.
without a shift, a change answers 428 and does nothing until confirmed; then it is recorded flagged.
inside the shift and the person's work, a change goes through without a question and is recorded.
inside the shift but not the person's kind of work: 428 with roleMismatch, then recorded flagged.
Managers read the record per person and the flagged changes; others' staff 404; Staff 403.
a Manager creates a Staff account for Blocks A and B; it is Invited and gets the set-password email; the email, name and Blocks are checked; Staff cannot create accounts.

a Manager renames a Staff member, changes the title and Blocks, disables the account (signed out) and restores it; Managers and Admins are not Staff accounts (404); an invitation is resent only while Invited.
emails remember whether their recipient is a fictional account: a seed account's are, a real person's are not, so only the first may go to the demo mailbox (spec O-3).
duty follows presence: signing in puts a person on duty, going idle or signing out takes them off, using the app again puts them back; nobody sets it by hand.
open work is split by kind, a Maintenance Request past its SLA counts as overdue.
an inspection run with the person as inspector counts as Inspection work.
a person is overloaded above {@code workload.max_open_per_staff}, not at it.
a swap waiting for Staff is in the Block's queue and in nobody's open count.
one person's open work is listed with the overdue items first.
the work of someone who shares no Block with the Manager is not found; Staff may not read it.
moving two items gives them to the receiver, audits each move and tells the receiver.
a receiver who does not handle the kind of work gets nothing: 422, no item moved.
when one item was closed meanwhile the whole move is refused: 409, nothing moved.
(BE-3RD-01): a Staff member taken off Block A gives Block A's open work back to its queue (nobody in charge, audited), so nothing is left with someone who can no longer reach it.
(BE-3RD-01): disabling a Staff member gives all their open work back to the Block queues.

(final review of BE-3RD-01): when the inspector is disabled, their schedule no longer names them (its next runs are nobody's) and the released run is open to the Block's Staff, the first to work on it takes it.
Managers list every student with filters and the count waiting for verification; Staff see only the residents of their Blocks; students may not list.
the student hub shows the profile, the account, the Bed, the Applications, Invoices and requests and the history; Staff open only residents of their Blocks; an unknown id is 404.
a Manager corrects directory fields; each is checked; the change is audited; Staff cannot edit.
a Manager verifies a pending account (the student is told) or rejects it (locked); locking signs the student out until a Manager unlocks the account; a rejected account comes back as pending.
only a verified account may apply: a pending one sees why and is refused (ADR-26).
(BE-3RD-09): a student who holds a Bed keeps their gender (Blocks and roommates were chosen by it); the other fields still change.

a student edits their phone and personal email, adds emergency contacts up to the limit, edits, reorders and removes them; the first contact is mirrored in the student record that Applications read, each field is checked, another student's contact is not found and only students have contacts.

the template names the columns; an upload is previewed line by line (New, Update, Unchanged, Error with the reason) and counts the students the file leaves out; nothing changes before the confirmation.

confirming creates and updates the accounts, verifies the waiting one that matches, gives a fictional student's code to the real student, marks real students missing from the file Not enrolled (never fictional ones), is written to the Audit Log and cannot run twice.

an XLSX workbook is read like a CSV (shared strings, dates as day numbers, Vietnamese headers); a file without a required column or not in UTF-8 is refused; lines can be filtered; Staff may not import.

a major is read from its code, its English label or its Vietnamese name, the other FPT majors are in the list (V61), and a student-code prefix such as SS put in the major column gets an error that says so; the file is the XLSX the template writer makes.
a direct swap of next-Term Beds: the partner accepts, Staff check and approve, the two next-Term Allocations exchange Beds while both students stay where they live this Term.
the swap board of the window: an anonymous post of a next-Term Bed with its next-Term price, a matching request, the swap without any charge or credit; a Bed the post does not want is refused.
a swap across Blocks goes from Staff to a Manager, who decides it last; once filing closed and the next-Term fees are issued no swap is carried out any more.

the dashboard of a Term shows its milestones in order with their progress, its Applications by status, the places per Room Type × Room Class × gender with the Term's prices, and the Deposits issued; Staff cannot read it and an unknown Term is 404.
a Manager files a request; it is Submitted with its proposal and history, every Admin and every other Manager is notified with a link to the requests list, and the requester is not.
(negative): missing fields and an unknown Block are named per field; a second open request for the same Term is refused; Staff and students cannot file or read requests.

another Manager comments (the requester and the Admin are told); the Admin asks for changes only with a note; the requester changes and sends it again; the Admin rejects it with a reason; a closed request takes no comment, and every step is in the history.

the Admin builds the Draft from a Manager's request: it holds the request's dates, Blocks, Rooms and prices, the request is In progress (the Manager is told) and building again opens the same Draft; a price that differs from the request needs a reason, which the request then shows next to the difference.

the Manager proposes prices as a base price per Room Type and a surcharge per Room Class (BR-10: the request computes each line, rounded up), offers one Room Type and one Room Class, and proposes the Deposit, Utility Deposit, the share for new students and the house rules (review R-02, R-03), starting from the defaults ({@code /term-requests/defaults}). The Draft built from it holds them all; the Admin's different Deposit needs a reason and is listed for the Manager; a surcharge above 500% is refused.
(negative): the Timeline step checks spec §5.2 per field: registration closing before it opens, renewal milestones filled in only partly or out of order, Check-in before the Term before is left.

a Draft with unsaved steps cannot be published; once every step is saved, publishing fixes the Term's prices, Deposit and rules, tells every Manager (Term dashboard link) and puts the Term announcement on the students' board and bell. A later default-price change leaves the Term's prices alone, an Application pays the Term's Deposit, and once an Invoice exists the prices are locked.

after publishing, a passed date is fixed and an open deadline is only extended; a change needs a reason and becomes a change announcement with old → new values (also in Vietnamese); the rules stay fixed.

(moved from TC-CFG-004 when the legacy create/update endpoints went, BE-3RD-08): a Draft is invisible to students until published; a second publish and a Term whose stay overlaps a published one are refused.

a Manager terminates a resident's stay with a reason: Notice sent with the move-out date, the student is told (in-app and email) and sees it on My Room, the desk lists the check-out; Staff read it but may not start or cancel; one termination at a time; a Manager cancels it with a reason and the student is told.

past the move-out date the termination is Overdue: Managers and the Block's Staff are told, the Room's door code must change and the student no longer sees it; the check-out closes the termination and refunds the unused room fee by its rule (Not enrolled 30 %, decided by a Manager).
an overdue Utility Invoice gives warning 1 (in-app and email), once; a second overdue month gives the final warning with the termination day (today + 3); paying everything closes both.

(business rule): from the termination day, two overdue months terminate the stay (notice to the student, the Managers' list); a debt reaching the Utility Deposit does too, even in its first month; with that rule off one month does not, and nothing happens before the termination day.
(BE-2ND-05): a Manager cancelling a Utility-debt termination gives the warnings back, with a new termination day, so the debt rule keeps working instead of staying silent for the rest of the stay.
(WEB-STU-22): Payments without a Term lists the unpaid Invoices first, so an older unpaid one is not pushed off the first page by newer paid ones.
a Manager sends next week's schedule: every Staff member of the Block is told; the week shows sent.
on Sunday from the reminder hour the Managers are reminded once; never on other days or earlier.
Admin chooses the reminder's day and hour in System parameters (or turns it off); the reminder follows them, and a day outside the list is refused.
a Manager plans a Staff member's next week without changing this week, can put it back to the default weekly shifts, and cannot plan a past week or a week too far ahead.
a Staff member sees next week's shifts only once a Manager sent their Block's schedule.
in or out of shift follows this week's plan, not the default weekly shifts.
what Staff handle follows the Staff portal; each Staff screen's changes belong to one kind.
exact texts and texts with values are translated, a value from the catalog too; English stays English.
a text without a translation, an unknown language and null are returned unchanged.
with a demo mailbox an email to a fictional account goes there, the recipient in the subject and a header.
without it the email goes to its recipient unchanged; without SMTP nothing is sent or thrown.
a real account receives its own email even while a demo mailbox is set (spec O-3).

(Wave 1 regression): BE-ASG-02: resolving an item must not place it in a Block that is already committed.
(Wave 1 regression): BE-ASG-04: when a proposed Bed was taken meanwhile, committing the Block does not fail as a whole with BED_TAKEN and nothing to resolve: the item becomes a conflict.
(Wave 1 regression): BE-ASG-05: a resident with an overdue termination cannot be moved (which would hand them a new Room).
(Wave 1 regression): BE-ASG-07: cancelling a termination keeps a check-out that was pending for another reason.
(Wave 1 regression): BE-AUTH-02: one client guessing passwords across many accounts is throttled (429) at some point.
(Wave 1 regression): BE-AUTH-02: a stranger's 5 wrong passwords must not lock the owner out (right password, other IP).
the limiter keys on the client address: one client's 100 failures do not throttle another client.
a shared network (school NAT): 30 failed sign-ins, then a correct password still signs in.
one account guessed from many clients (or spoofed addresses) is still capped: 30 failures lock it.
(Wave 1 regression): BE-AUTH-03: anonymous forgot-password requests from one client across many accounts are throttled.
(Wave 1 regression): BE-PLT-10: a JSON endpoint called with a wrong content type answers 415/400, not 500 INTERNAL_ERROR.
(Wave 1 regression): BE-APP-BIL-01: Staff must not read Block Finance, Invoices or refunds (with students' bank accounts).
(Wave 1 regression): BE-APP-BIL-02: deciding refunds is Managers only (Permission.DECIDE_REFUNDS), also for a check-out refund.
(Wave 1 regression): BE-APP-BIL-03: after the transfer a Manager can mark an approved refund Paid.
a refund is marked paid once; a second call (double submit) gets 409 REFUND_NOT_APPROVED.

(Wave 1 regression): BE-APP-BIL-04: an Application rejected (not enrolled) while its Deposit claim waits: once a Manager confirms that claim the money must be refunded (or the claim must have been withdrawn).
(Wave 1 regression): BE-APP-BIL-05: the current month cannot be closed before it ends (409 PERIOD_NOT_ENDED).
(Wave 1 regression): BE-APP-BIL-06: an office rejection refunds the whole Deposit, whatever the student-cancellation rule says.
(BE-PLT-06): six more recipients add only their own writes (the email and the notification), not a read of the Block, the Invoices, the template, the language and the demo flag each.
(Wave 1 regression): WEB-ADM-02: the RENEWAL_UNDECIDED notification links to an existing Manager route.

(Wave 1 regression): BE-PLT-01: a request whose stored deadline (sla_due_at, e.g. the urgent 4-hour timer) passed before it was resolved is late, even if it was resolved within the Block's normal 48-hour timer.
(Wave 1 regression): BE-PLT-11: with no Block chosen the floor chart must not sum floor N of every Block into one bar.
(Wave 1 regression): BE-2ND-01: a resident who holds the door code but never had a desk check-in (a continuing resident, or handover off) can still be checked out.
(Wave 1 regression): BE-2ND-02: two "Complete check-out" submits at once settle the check-out once (one meter cut).

(Wave 1 regression): BE-ASG-03: a shared item's damage split among 3 residents at check-out is charged to the roommates who lived with it, not to whoever lives in the Room when a Manager keeps the line a week later.
(BE-OPS-09): a resident's in-stay furniture report shows on My Room and at the check-out desk.
(BE-ASG-10): a shared item's damage split among 3 residents invoices each roommate full/3 (rounded down).
(Wave 1 regression): BE-OPS-01: once the student also holds a next-Term Allocation (from M2), a furniture report still attaches to the Allocation of the current stay, the one the check-out reads.
a signed link opens the file with nosniff; a changed sig, another id or a past exp is 404.
(BE-2ND-03): a Block whose Beds a live run proposes cannot change gender.
(BE-3RD-04): a Room whose Bed a live run proposes cannot be set out of service.
(BE-2ND-04): a Room Class the Term's frozen price table does not offer is refused (NO_PRICE).
(BE-3RD-02): a furniture type the Admin never priced is not charged at an invented price.
(BE-3RD-03): a Room Class made Inactive keeps its frozen price in a published Term.
(Wave 1 regression): BE-PLT-02: an "assistant" turn the server never returned (forged by the client) must not reach the model.
an assistant turn with a signature the server did not make (another key, or edited text) is dropped.
(Wave 1 regression): BE-PLT-04: one data section failing with a non-API exception must not break every answer with a 500.
(Wave 1 regression): BE-PLT-07: a campaign whose group is not lower-case ("Residents") passes validation; send must not 500.
(Wave 1 regression): BE-PLT-08: a template body the Admin may save (1000 chars) plus a reject note (500 chars) must not roll back the Manager's rejection.
(Wave 1 regression): BE-PLT-09: shortening the stay below the saved Check-in in step 1 gets a field message (400), not a 409.
(M6): an assistant turn the server signed for one student is dropped when another student sends it (the signature covers the account as well as the text).
(Wave 1 regression): BE-OPS-02: "Offer temporary Bed" must do something: at least the student is told.
(Wave 1 regression): BE-OPS-03: the Block's Room-change timer (24 h) sets the new Room-Change Request's deadline.
(Wave 1 regression): BE-OPS-04: routing rules can only be created for kinds that are routed (Maintenance, Room change).
(Wave 1 regression): BE-OPS-05: the scan escalates on the stored deadline, not on reported_at + today's timer.
(Wave 1 regression): BE-OPS-06: Staff cannot close a Submitted, unassigned request directly.
(Wave 1 regression): BE-ASG-06 (uses the requests window, hence here): cancelling an OVERDUE termination either is refused or gives back the next-Term Bed that becoming overdue took away.
My Room shows the longest stay allowed, so the extension options come from the server (WEB-STU-06).
(Wave 1 regression): BE-ASG-09: a resident whose Bed is already taken in the next Term at M2 is told (not only an audit line).

(Wave 1 regression): BE-OPS-07: a Manager's bulk approval keeps a Block A student in Block A when a matching Bed is free there, even if another male Block's Bed (Block "0", partly filled) sorts first.
(Wave 1 regression): BE-OPS-08: a Block timer above the Admin's lowered limit is capped by it.
(BE-2ND-06): when Staff move a student's next-Term Allocation to another Bed, the room change the student filed from the old one closes instead of staying open on an Allocation that no longer exists.
(M5): a resident who already holds a next-Term Bed elsewhere (placed before M2) is not told that their Bed was taken: the conflict is on the student, not on the Bed.

an exact origin and a Vercel preview pattern are both admitted.
(negative): other origins are refused, and a blank setting keeps CORS closed.
an invited pair shares an empty 2-bed Room; the next student gets NO_BED when none is left.
a student who is no longer eligible is flagged and never placed.
an invited partner who is not in the run blocks the pair (PARTNER_NOT_READY).
a single student joins the Room whose occupant shares the most attributes.
the priority group goes first; the same input gives the same proposal.
a placement with few shared attributes is kept and marked LOW_FIT (information only).
Good and Worn count as the same, and meters within the tolerance match.
one item reported Damaged where the record says Good is a minor difference.
an item the record had in the Room reported Missing needs a visit.
three differing items need a visit.
the meter limit grows with the hours since the reading and the residents.
items the record does not know are never a difference.
the chat is posted unstreamed with the model, the context size and the proxy key; the answer is read.
a missing model (404) or an unreachable server answers 503 ASSISTANT_OFFLINE.
the code is posted with the popup redirect URI and the ID token is returned.
a code of the redirect flow (popup blocked) is exchanged with the sign-in page as redirect URI.
(negative): a used or expired code is the user's retryable error (401).
(negative): a wrong client secret is our misconfiguration, not the user's (503).
(negative): Google cannot be reached (503).
(boundary): without a client secret the code flow is off and Google is never called.
a token with the FPT hd and a verified email is accepted.
a missing or wrong hd, or an unverified email, is 403 GOOGLE_DOMAIN_NOT_ALLOWED.
a token for another client (aud) or from another issuer is GOOGLE_TOKEN_INVALID.
an unknown FPT Google account signs up as a student without a password; until it sets one only the setup endpoints answer; the password follows the usual rules and is set once.
the sign-up form checks every field and the student code; once sent the account is Pending verification, every Manager is told, and the student cannot apply.

an address ending with the code of an imported, unused account signs in to that account (Verified, linked to Google); a fictional account's code is never matched, and a real student who needs it takes it.
a rejected account cannot sign in, and the answer gives the Manager's reason.
(security): a fictional back-office account of the seed signs in with its password only, so whoever owns that address at FPT cannot take its role through Google; a real staff account still can.
every Block gets this month's period; a month ended more than {@code utility.close_days} ago and still open is shown on the Staff and Manager Overviews, and its Block's Staff are reminded once a day.
residents who lived in the Room the whole month pay equal shares.
a check-out cuts the meter; the leaver's share is marked settled (paid from the Utility Deposit).
within a segment, shares follow the time each resident lived in the Room; totals round up.
without a reading at the end there is nothing to share yet.
a failing SMTP send counts an attempt, moves not_before later, and stops as FAILED at the maximum.
a signed service-account JWT buys an access token; the message goes to the device.
an unregistered device token is reported so it can be disabled; other errors are failures.
the JWT is RS256-signed with the service account key and names the FCM scope.
quoting, empty cells, campus times, and text a spreadsheet would run as a formula.

parseDecimal reads vi and en formats
a lone separator followed by exactly three digits is ambiguous (M1)

the notification that started the app and later taps open their links
nothing opens when no notification was tapped
helpers the schedule joins the registration window and marks the current row
helpers time left, due dates and furniture lines read like the web
money, days and instants read like the web
